title: Getting the most out of Codex
summary: Maximilian Schwarzmüller on using Codex alongside Claude Code: desktop app review comments, plan mode, explicit context, skills, concise AGENTS.md, staying in control.

assertions.quote: I still don't loop. I don't use the Rolf loop thing ... I stay in control

verdicts.note: Goal/loop features keep agents going through backlogs, but unattended runs drift or game checks without good verification; works when acceptance tests are strong.

assertions.quote: planning still matters ... I'm using that all the time

verdicts.note: Plan-then-execute consistently reduces agent rework in practice and in vendor evals, especially on multi-file tasks.

assertions.quote: if you do know that a certain file will matter ... you wanna point your agent at it

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: They're lazily loaded ... only the metadata is loaded into the context window

verdicts.note: Skills load only short descriptions until used, and deferred tool loading cuts context; this is how Claude Code, Manus and others manage large capability sets.

assertions.quote: You're responsible for your code. It's not the AI, it's you

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.
The paper recommends careful review of AI code whatever the tool, along with static analysis, tests, security checks, and monitoring after merge.

assertions.quote: always make sure ... that you don't detach from it ... and then you're essentially forced to do vibe coding

verdicts.note: Ignoring code entirely leads to drift and debt in real codebases; but spec-driven approaches with code review do work.

assertions.quote: use that agents.md file to your advantage. Keep it concise

verdicts.note: Persistent instruction files measurably steer agent behavior; overlong or contradictory ones reduce adherence.

assertions.quote: you wanna give these tools ways of verifying their own work

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.
